html:
An Arab nationalist and socialist party founded in Damascus in 1947. Ba'ath means rebirth. Its branches later ruled Syria and Iraq for decades.

Its founders were two Damascus schoolteachers educated in Paris, the Christian Michel Aflaq and the Sunni Muslim Salah al-Din al-Bitar, together with followers of the thinker Zaki al-Arsuzi. Its slogan was "Unity, Freedom, Socialism": all Arabs were one nation that should form one state, free of colonial rule, with land reform and state planning. It spread among students, teachers and army officers in Syria, Iraq, Jordan and Lebanon.

The party pushed Syria into the United Arab Republic with Egypt in 1958, which broke up in 1961. In 1963 Ba'athist officers seized power in both Syria and Iraq. The two branches split in 1966 and became bitter rivals.

  • In Iraq the party ruled from 1968 to 2003, under Saddam Hussein from 1979. After the US invasion it was banned.
  • In Syria Hafez al-Assad took over in 1970 and his son Bashar ruled after him. Its rule ended when Bashar al-Assad fell in December 2024.

In both countries the party's ideals gave way to one-man rule, the secret police and family and sect networks.
sum: An Arab nationalist and socialist party founded in Damascus in 1947. Ba'ath means rebirth. Its branches later ruled Syria and Iraq for decades.
